name: Xero Ledger Airlock - an approval binds to the ledger state you reviewed
description:
Governed Xero for teams too small for a compliance function. 13 commands across invoices, payments, the chart of accounts and overdue-invoice chasing. Every write is held behind the airlock and sealed into a signed receipt.

THE IDEA: Xero validates the write. It does not validate that the write is still the one you approved. Between the moment you review a batch and the moment it commits, a payment can land, an invoice can be recoded, a period can close - and the resulting write is still legal, so nothing stops it. This module refuses it.

Every apply command re-reads the ledger, recomputes a fingerprint covering totals, amounts paid and every line item's account code, and refuses the whole batch on any drift - naming what moved. The approval binds to the plan's CONTENT, not to a filename.

WHAT IT DOES NOT CLAIM: Xero refuses a void on a paid invoice and refuses an overpayment by itself. On those, this module is defence in depth - it refuses earlier, at plan time, so you never approve something that cannot succeed. It says so in the command output rather than implying it is the only guard.

DUNNING (v0.1.2): plan_send_reminder and apply_send_reminder chase an overdue invoice as a sequence rather than an event. Xero applies NO deduplication to invoice emails - probed live, five sends produced five deliveries - so the module keeps its own hash-chained dunning record, and that record is the only thing preventing a re-run from emailing a customer twice. The plan refuses at plan time on every rule the API enforces at send time: no email address on the contact, an invoice that is not AUTHORISED, and a stage already sent. It sends one rung of the ladder per run, so a workflow that has not run for a fortnight catches up one reminder at a time instead of delivering two in a day. A part-payment holds the current stage for one cycle without resetting the ladder. The email body is Xero's own standard invoice template - this governs WHEN a customer is chased and when the chase stops, not what the message says.

commands.title: Preflight: which reads this token can perform, and what it cannot prove
commands.description: Probes each scope group with one cheap read and reports what the API refused. Xero publishes no granted-scope set, so this is inference, never introspection. Also reports the tenant list, the connection id, live rate-limit quota and when the refresh token last rotated.

commands.title: The codes every other command needs: accounts, tax rates, lock dates
commands.description: Writes the chart of accounts, tax rates, tracking categories and the organisation's period lock dates to a file. Output is almost entirely ids and codes, which a receipt would redact, so the operator gets a path.

commands.title: What is quietly rotting, each finding naming the command that fixes it

draft_days.description: flag DRAFT invoices older than this (default 14)

overdue_days.description: flag AUTHORISED invoices overdue past this (default 1)

max_findings.description: refuse past this many rather than truncate (default 1000)

commands.description: Scans for drafts past N days, overdue authorised invoices bucketed for dunning, overpaid invoices, and contacts missing a default account or tax type. Every finding names the governed command that would fix it.

commands.title: Re-walk the local write ledger and report the first break
commands.description: Hash-chain integrity check over every applied write and every refusal this module recorded. Tamper-evident, not tamper-proof: it detects edits and mid-chain deletion, not truncation of the tail by whoever holds the file.

commands.title: Resolve invoices to an explicit list and fingerprint it

invoice_ids.description: explicit InvoiceID list; overrides the selector

max_invoices.description: refuse past this many rather than truncate (default 200)

commands.description: Resolves a selector to an explicit invoice list with current totals, tax, amounts due and every line item's account code, then writes a plan file carrying a two-level fingerprint. Reads only; nothing is posted.

commands.title: Authorise an approved batch, refusing on any drift

plan_path.description: path to the file the matching plan_ command wrote

plan_fp.description: the plan's fingerprint, copied from the plan command's output or the plan file. Binds the approval to plan CONTENT, not to a filename. Accepted with or without the display grouping

composite_fp.description: optional cross-system fingerprint for a multi-module transaction coordinator

commands.description: Re-reads every invoice in the plan, recomputes the fingerprint, and refuses the WHOLE batch on any drift, naming the offending invoice. Uses summarizeErrors=false and reads the per-element verdict, because Xero returns HTTP 200 with per-element failures inside it. This is the point of no return: an AUTHORISED invoice can no longer be deleted, only voided.

commands.title: Report why each invoice is or is not voidable
commands.description: For each candidate: status, amount paid, amount due, the full payment list, allocated credit notes, and whether the invoice date falls inside a locked period. States for each one whether it is voidable and why not.

commands.title: Void an approved batch, refusing on any drift

plan_path.description: path to the file the matching plan_ command wrote

plan_fp.description: the plan's fingerprint, copied from the plan command's output or the plan file. Binds the approval to plan CONTENT, not to a filename. Accepted with or without the display grouping

composite_fp.description: optional cross-system fingerprint for a multi-module transaction coordinator

commands.description: Re-reads every invoice, refuses if a payment landed since plan, if AmountPaid moved at all, if a credit note was allocated, if the status changed, or if the period closed. Xero itself refuses a void on a paid invoice; this refuses earlier and names what changed.

commands.title: Snapshot balances and flag any allocation that would overpay

allocations.description: [{invoice_id, amount, date}] - date defaults to today

account_id.description: AccountID of the bank account to pay from

commands.description: Resolves explicit (invoice, amount, date, account) tuples, snapshots each invoice's AmountDue and AmountPaid, shows resulting balances, and flags any allocation exceeding the amount due before an operator approves it.

commands.title: Record approved payments, refusing on any drift

plan_path.description: path to the file the matching plan_ command wrote

plan_fp.description: the plan's fingerprint, copied from the plan command's output or the plan file. Binds the approval to plan CONTENT, not to a filename. Accepted with or without the display grouping

composite_fp.description: optional cross-system fingerprint for a multi-module transaction coordinator

commands.description: Re-reads every invoice and refuses on drift in AmountDue AND in AmountPaid. A rising AmountPaid means a payment landed while the allocation sat in review. Unlike a posted invoice, a payment recorded here can be deleted afterwards - this is the one reversible write in the module.

commands.title: The contact book with reachability, in one paged read

max_contacts.description: refuse past this many rather than truncate (default 2000)

only_reachable.description: artifact carries only contacts holding an email address (default false) — pass true/false (declared with no type: the airlock's validator has no boolean branch and refuses any value for a field declared boolean)

commands.description: Reads the whole contact book in one paged call and reports how many contacts can actually be emailed. The recipient address is never on an invoice payload, so a dunning plan cannot be built without this. Counts an empty EmailAddress and a missing EmailAddress key alike as no address - Xero returns both shapes and a key-presence test would call unreachable contacts reachable. Also surfaces the sales default account code and receivable tax type that hygiene_scan flags as missing but cannot show.

commands.title: Which overdue invoices are owed this reminder stage, and which are not

stage.description: the ladder rung to plan, in days overdue (e.g. 7). Must be a member of ladder

ladder.description: the escalation ladder in days overdue (default [7, 21, 45]). Never hardcode a threshold in a caller

invoice_ids.description: restrict to these invoices; omit to consider every AUTHORISED sales invoice

max_invoices.description: refuse past this many rather than truncate (default 200)

allow_empty_greeting.description: send to a contact with no personal first name, whose email would open 'Hi ,' (default false — such contacts are refused at plan time) — pass true/false (declared with no type: the airlock's validator has no boolean branch and refuses any value for a field declared boolean)

commands.description: Builds a plan containing ONLY the invoices that can actually be sent this stage, and records why every excluded one was excluded. Refuses at plan time on all three rules probed live against Xero: a contact with no email address, an invoice that is not AUTHORISED, and a stage this invoice has already been sent. Enforces one rung per run - an invoice forty days overdue with nothing sent is owed stage 7, not stage 21, and never both in one run. A part-payment holds the current stage for one cycle without resetting the ladder.

commands.description: Re-reads every invoice and re-reads the dunning record before sending anything, then refuses the WHOLE batch if any invoice drifted or if any stage has been sent since the plan was approved. Xero applies no deduplication to invoice emails - five sends produce five deliveries - so this record is the only guard, and an email cannot be recalled.
